problem.title_as_question: Why should players swing around rather than low-to-high?
problem.definition: Players often try to create topspin and height by linearly lifting the entire racket and arm upward ('low-to-high'), which breaks natural shoulder rotation and prevents high-speed topspin generation.
prerequisites: Player understands basic forehand topspin mechanics and wants to generate aggressive pace and spin through rotational mechanics.

symptoms.description: The racket does not roll around down past the hand during finish; the entire arm/racket system is lifted up vertically.
Finish shows elbow down with forearm rolled, rather than elbow up with racket down.
Ball sprays crosscourt or misses off to the left due to over-rotating the trunk all the way to target.
Executing proper shoulder roll feels counterintuitively like hitting downward or into the ground.

causes.statement: Player's brain mentally focuses on swinging up to produce height and spin, preventing the shoulder from releasing into internal rotation around.
Player linearly drags the elbow across the body and relies solely on forearm rolling instead of loading and rolling the entire shoulder.
Ball is spaced too close to the body, forcing a linear shoulder push rather than allowing room for the arm/shoulder to roll out to the right.
Accelerating the trunk all the way through to the target rather than decelerating early short of the target to let the shoulder release.

angles.summary: The shoulder loads into external rotation with back/scapular stabilization and releases through into protraction and internal rotation.
The rolling action travels in a circle ('around'); during the forward segment of that circle, it is travelling upward across the ball.
When done correctly without lifting the whole racket system, the stroke feels like hitting down into the ground.
When the trunk slows down, the shoulder whips off naturally; the trunk must accelerate short of the target and brake.
Rafael Nadal hits knee-high balls with only about 6 inches of upward elbow movement, generating massive lift purely through shoulder and racket rotation.

solutions.summary: Feed or set up balls farther out to the hitting side so the player has room to lean over the hitting foot and release the shoulder around into external-to-internal rotation.
solutions.external_goal: Set contact spacing significantly farther out to your right.

solutions.summary: Ensure the butt cap sits in the palm with the pinky finger resting on the flare of the butt cap to maximize the topspin lever.
solutions.external_goal: Keep the butt cap nestled into the palm with the pinky on the flare.

solutions.summary: Accelerate the trunk in a compact range of motion short of the intended target line, then decelerate the trunk to let the shoulder and arm crack off toward the target.
solutions.external_goal: Stop/slow the trunk rotation before reaching the target line.
